transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

You are absolutely correct: a standard tumble dryer should not be using or draining water during a drying cycle.

If you hear water running in and out while on a drying-only program, there is likely one of three issues at play. Here’s how to troubleshoot your Beko dryer:

### 1. Check if You Accidentally Selected a "Wash & Dry" or "Hygiene" Program
Some modern Beko models (especially washer-dryers or advanced dryers) have programs that involve steaming, sanitizing, or refreshing clothes using water.
• Look at the display: Did you select a program like "Steam Refresh," "Anti-Allergy," "Cotton Care with Steam," or "Wash & Dry"?
• Solution: Ensure you’ve selected a standard drying cycle like "Cottons Dry," "Synthetics," or "Time Dry." These should use only air and heat.

### 2. The Dryer Is Actually a Washer-Dryer (Washer-Drier Combo)
If your appliance is a washer-dryer combo (one machine that both washes and dries), it may have residual water in the drum from a previous wash cycle if you didn’t drain it properly.
• Check: Did you run a wash cycle before this? If so, did it complete fully? Sometimes combos get stuck or error out, leaving water behind.
• Solution: Run a "Drain & Spin" or "Drain Only" program first to remove any leftover water before starting the drying cycle.

### 3. There Is a Fault with the Water Inlet Valve or Control Board (Less Common but Possible)
If you are certain you selected a standard drying-only program and it’s not a washer-dryer combo, then there is a fault:
• Water Inlet Valve Stuck Open: The valve that lets water in for steam functions may be stuck open due to debris or a mechanical failure.
• Control Board Error: The electronic board may be sending incorrect signals, activating the water inlet when it shouldn’t.
• Drain Pump Running Continuously: If the drain pump is running but no water is entering, you might just hear the pump cycling due to a sensor error (e.g., thinking there’s water in the drum when there isn’t).

### Immediate Steps to Take:
1. Stop the machine immediately and turn it off at the wall socket.
2. Check your program selection: Confirm you’re not using a steam or hygiene cycle.
3. Inspect for leaks: Look under the machine for any water pooling, which would confirm water is entering.
4. Run a drain-only cycle: If available on your Beko model, run a "Drain" program to clear any residual water.
5. Check the filter: Clean the lint filter and check the condenser unit (if it’s a condenser dryer) for blockages. A blocked system can sometimes cause strange sensor errors.

### When to Call a Technician:
• If you’re sure you selected a standard drying program and water is still entering/draining, it’s a hardware fault.
• Contact Beko Customer Support or a qualified appliance repair technician. Do not continue using the machine, as it could waste significant amounts of water or cause electrical issues if water leaks into internal components.

Note: If your model number starts with something like "DWQ" or "WDQ," it’s likely a washer-dryer combo, and step #2 above is the most probable cause. If it’s a standard dryer (model numbers often start with "D" followed by letters/numbers without "W"), then it’s almost certainly a faulty valve or control board.

Thank you. It's a washer-dryer, model WDL742431W, only 2 months old. I selected a drying-only programme, no error codes, and the clothes do come out dry. There's no water on the floor either. Is this really a fault, or is it normal?

Given that your Beko WDL742431W is only 2 months old, you selected a drying-only program, there are no error codes, and the clothes come out dry without any leaks, this is likely not a fault but rather a feature of how this specific washer-dryer model operates.

Here’s why:

### 1. Washer-Dryers Use Water for Condensation Management
Unlike standalone tumble dryers that only use air and heat, washer-dryers (especially condenser models like your Beko) often use small amounts of water during the drying cycle to help manage condensation and maintain efficiency. This is particularly true in certain programs or if the ambient temperature is low. The water helps cool the condenser coils more effectively, allowing the machine to dry clothes faster and more efficiently while using less energy than a pure air-based system might in some conditions.

### 2. The "Wash & Dry" Cycle Logic
Even when you select a "Drying Only" program on a washer-dryer, the internal logic may still involve brief water usage for:
• Condenser Cooling: To keep the condenser at the optimal temperature for moisture extraction.
• Drum Rinse/Refresh: Some models use a small amount of water to rinse lint or residues from the drum before drying begins.
• Steam Function Activation: If your model has automatic steam features activated by default in certain programs, it may introduce water even in "drying-only" modes unless explicitly disabled.

### 3. Why It’s Not Leaking
The fact that there’s no water on the floor and the machine drains properly confirms that the water is being used internally and drained correctly as part of the cycle. This is normal operation for a washer-dryer.

### What You Can Do:
• Check the Manual: Look up your specific model (WDL742431W) in the user manual under the "Drying" or "Programs" section. It may explicitly state that water usage occurs during drying cycles for condensation management.
• Try a Different Program: Select a simple "Time Dry" or "Synthetics Dry" program and see if you still hear water running. If it stops, then certain programs (like Cottons or Hygiene) are using water intentionally.
• Monitor Performance: Since the clothes come out dry and there are no errors, the machine is functioning as designed.

### When to Be Concerned:
If you notice any of the following, contact Beko support (you’re still under warranty):
• Water leaking onto the floor.
• Error codes appearing on the display.
• Clothes not drying properly despite the cycle completing.
• Unusual noises or vibrations beyond normal operation.

For now, since your machine is working correctly and is under warranty, you can likely continue using it as-is. If the water usage bothers you, try switching to a simpler drying program like "Time Dry" to see if that reduces or eliminates the water sound.

Thank you. I looked in the manual as you suggested, and it does say that water is used during drying for condensation. So I take it this is normal and not a fault? I'd just like to be sure it isn't something that will wear the machine out early.

Yes, you can rest assured that this is normal operation and not a fault. It is highly unlikely to cause premature wear or damage to your machine if used as intended.

Here’s why:

### 1. Designed for This Purpose
Your Beko WDL742431W is engineered to use small amounts of water during drying cycles specifically for condensation management. The internal components (valves, pumps, and condensers) are built to handle this routine usage without excessive wear. This feature helps the machine dry clothes more efficiently and effectively than a pure air-based system would in many conditions.
